title: ComplaintScope Data Ingestion and Quality Funnel
observation: Initial pool of 878,262 narratives was filtered to 19,998 complaints; 131,442 exact duplicates removed.
inference: Exact duplicate removal and word count thresholds successfully eliminate boilerplate noise without distorting macro distribution.
limitation: Filtering retains only opt-in narrative complaints; does not represent the non-narrative complaint majority.

title: Temporal Trajectory of Consumer Complaints Over Time
observation: Monthly complaint volume demonstrates pronounced upward surges following early 2020 economic disruptions and forbearance policies.
inference: External macro events (CARES Act, pandemic stimulus, debt freezes) drove substantial shifts in consumer reporting behavior.
limitation: Sampling was drawn proportionally to monthly volume; seasonal dips reflect raw database arrival rates.

title: Harmonised Product Class Distribution in Modelling Sample
observation: Credit reporting & repair and Debt collection constitute the largest classes (51.2% and 15.7%).
inference: Severe class imbalance requires macro-averaged F1 and class-weighted optimization for equitable routing evaluation.
limitation: CFPB's taxonomy consolidation combined pre-2017 and post-2017 definitions, creating label boundary artifacts.

title: Distribution of Narrative Word Lengths Across Complaints
observation: Distribution is heavily right-skewed with median length 136 words and mean 200 words.
inference: Sublinear TF scaling and vocabulary frequency cutoffs are critical to prevent long narratives from dominating TF-IDF weights.
limitation: Truncation at 256 tokens for sentence embeddings will discard tail tokens in approximately 25% of longer complaints.

title: Consumer Relief Outcome Rates Across Product Classes
observation: Checking/savings and Credit cards exhibit relief rates > 20%, whereas Credit reporting & repair exhibits under 10% relief.
inference: Product category strongly conditions relief likelihood, confirming need for product-stratified calibration and metadata inclusion.
limitation: Relief is self-reported by institutions; banks frequently resolve disputed fees quickly compared to credit bureaus.

title: Chronological Dataset Partition Timeline and Split Boundaries
inference: Strict calendar partitioning prevents lookahead bias and guarantees realistic evaluation of emerging topics and classifier drift.
limitation: Models tested on late-2022/2023 complaints must generalize across macroeconomic interest rate hikes and post-stimulus shifts.

title: Preprocessing Ablation Benchmark Across 7 Text Pipelines
observation: Champion 'No Redaction' pipeline achieves Macro-F1 = 0.5140 on validation, vs 0.4203 for minimal pipeline (+9.37pp gain).
inference: Preserving CFPB redaction markers as structural tokens provides informative positional context for downstream classifiers.
limitation: Ablation evaluated on fast logistic regression probe; rank ordering could subtly differ for non-linear deep transformers.

title: Empirical Rank-Frequency Fit vs Theoretical Zipf Power Law
observation: Log-log rank-frequency plot demonstrates linear decay with power law exponent alpha ~ 1.05.
inference: Confirms heavy-tailed Zipfian dynamics; min_df=5 and max_df=0.75 thresholds safely prune rare noise without truncating substantive head terms.
limitation: Domain-specific financial legal jargon produces slight curvature deviation at rank > 5,000.

title: Class-Specific Discriminative Term Importance by Log Odds / Chi-Square
observation: Clear semantic segregation: 'mortgage/escrow' for mortgages, 'inquiry/experian' for credit repair, 'overdraft/deposit' for banking.
inference: TF-IDF features provide highly distinct lexical signatures across primary CFPB categories.
limitation: Polysemous terms like 'account' or 'fee' bridge across multiple banking categories without context.

title: 2D UMAP Semantic Manifold Projection of Complaint Embeddings
observation: Compact distinct clusters for Student Loans and Mortgages; overlap between Credit Reporting and Debt Collection.
inference: Embedding geometry captures legal and regulatory overlap between credit reporting errors and third-party debt collection disputes.
limitation: 2D dimensionality reduction introduces topological crowding and metric distortion for high-dimensional 384-d vectors.

title: Normalized Confusion Matrix of Champion LinearSVC Model
observation: High diagonal concentration (overall accuracy 87.43%); primary off-diagonal confusion occurs between Debt collection and Credit reporting.
inference: Classifier mirrors real-world ambiguity where consumer disputes often involve both collection agencies and credit bureau reporting.
limitation: Payday loan class has smaller support, resulting in higher variance in normalized error percentages.

title: Reliability Calibration Diagram for Relief-Risk Probabilities
observation: Calibrated Logistic Regression closely traces the diagonal identity line, achieving Brier Score = 0.2316.
inference: Predicted probabilities are statistically reliable confidence estimates, suitable for regulatory prioritization.
limitation: Extreme probability deciles (> 0.8) exhibit slight under-confidence due to sparse positive density.

title: Precision-Recall Trajectory of Relief-Risk Prediction
observation: Achieves PR-AUC = 0.3865, substantially exceeding the naive baseline prior rate of 0.3170.
inference: Model extracts genuine signal from complaint narrative text and operational metadata under class imbalance.
limitation: Absolute precision ceilings exist due to unobserved internal institutional policies governing relief.

title: Operational Triage Lift and Cumulative Gain Curve
observation: Auditing top 5% highest-risk complaints yields 44.67% precision (1.41x lift over random); top 10% yields 42.86% (1.35x lift).
inference: Enables regulatory enforcement to prioritize immediate relief opportunities with 41% higher efficiency than random audit.
limitation: Triage curves assume complaint review capacity scales linearly with reviewer allocation.

title: Topic Model Coherence and Diversity Optimization Across K Topics
observation: Coherence c_v peaks at k=16 (c_v = 0.5009, diversity = 0.7312) before plateauing and decaying at k=24.
inference: K=16 identifies optimal granularity balancing semantic distinctness against redundant sub-topic fragmentation.
limitation: Coherence scores vary with sliding window size in reference corpus evaluation.

title: Topic-Product Conditional Probability Association Heatmap
observation: Strong diagonal association: Topic 3 aligns to Mortgages, Topic 7 to Checking/Savings, Topic 1 to Credit Inquiries.
inference: Unsupervised topics autonomously reconstruct latent statutory products while discovering granular cross-cutting issues.
limitation: Some shared transactional topics (billing dispute, customer service) disperse across multiple products.

title: Multi-Topic Temporal Burst Trajectories and Anomaly Flags
observation: Distinct spikes identified in early 2020 (CARES Act forbearance) and mid-2021 (credit repair disputes).
inference: Dual EWMA-CUSUM and rolling Z-score detectors flag acute spikes and sustained shifts concurrently.
limitation: Monthly aggregation bins introduce up to 30 days of detection latency compared to daily streams.

title: Proxy Burst Trajectory: COVID-19 Relief and Stimulus Inquiries
observation: CUSUM flags anomalous surge in March 2020 (+2 months before peak volume), reaching CUSUM-F1 = 0.7568.
inference: Confirms early-warning capability of cumulative sum tracking for sudden macroeconomic shocks.
limitation: Keyword proxy definition relies on retrospective lexicon of pandemic terms.

title: Proxy Burst Trajectory: CARES Act Mortgage Forbearance Disputes
observation: Rolling Z-score achieves Precision = 1.000; EWMA-CUSUM achieves F1 = 0.8000.
inference: High fidelity detection with zero false positive alarms during non-crisis baseline periods.
limitation: Forbearance terms experienced rapid post-moratorium decay, reducing late-period burst activity.

title: Proxy Burst Trajectory: Bank Overdraft and NSF Fee Disputes
observation: Consistent baseline volume with isolated post-holiday spikes; Z-score Precision = 1.000.
inference: Distinguishes structural fee complaints from transient seasonal liquidity crunches.
limitation: Multiple bank policy changes across 2021-2022 created confounding micro-bursts.

title: Proxy Burst Trajectory: Automated Credit Inquiries and Reporting Discrepancies
observation: Continuous upward baseline trend beginning in 2021; CUSUM accumulator flags sustained regulatory drift.
inference: EWMA-CUSUM effectively monitors chronic structural volume escalation that standard rolling Z-scores miss.
limitation: High overall volume dampens rolling Z-score sensitivity due to elevated baseline standard deviation.

title: Proxy Burst Trajectory: Third-Party Debt Collection and Verification
observation: Periodic cyclical burst alerts corresponding to CFPB Regulation F implementation in late 2021.
inference: Captures consumer pushback and compliance friction following major debt collection rule updates.
limitation: Debt collection encompasses heterogeneous sub-issues (medical, credit card, auto) under one umbrella.

title: Top Company Co-Occurrence Network and Louvain Community Structure
observation: Network exhibits 3 distinct Louvain communities (Modularity Q=0.2568, null model mean 0.0671, p < 0.001).
inference: Companies cluster strongly by financial sector: Credit Bureaus, Retail Mega-Banks, and Debt Collection Specialists.
limitation: Projection restricted to top 100 companies by complaint volume to maintain graphical readability.

title: Composite Systemic Risk Index (SRI) Ranking of Top Financial Institutions
observation: The Big 3 credit bureaus dominate SRI: TransUnion (0.7819), Experian (0.7187), Equifax (0.6825).
inference: Massive complaint volume combined with low consumer relief rates (< 10%) produces acute systemic consumer harm.
limitation: Composite score combines distinct dimensions; weights reflect regulatory judgment.

title: Dirichlet Weight Sensitivity and Rank Stability Distribution
observation: 100 Dirichlet perturbations yield mean Kendall's tau = 0.6374 +/- 0.2321; top-tier rankings remain highly robust.
inference: SRI prioritization is structurally resilient to subjective regulatory weighting choices.
limitation: Middle-tier institutions with closely matching composite scores exhibit moderate rank permutations under extreme weights.
